title: Instrumented probe adaptation for SLO-driven autoscaler stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an adaptive probe layer that tunes readiness/liveness sampling and gating thresholds using live SLO signals and recent latency distributions to reduce unnecessary autoscaler churn and prevent cascading load-shedding during regional failovers. This ticket implements the control loop, simulation harness, and a safe canary rollout path.

Why: We frequently observe oscillation in node pool size and frequent degraded-mode activations during transient latencies or cross-region ingress shifts. Current probes are static and tuned for worst-case bursts which causes overreactive scaling and poor SLO adherence during failover windows. An instrumented, SLO-aware probe adaptation will reduce flapping, improve tail latency adherence, and make circuit breakers less likely to trigger incorrectly.
background:
Observations from recent incidents: 2025-11 regional failover (postmortem) and multiple canary rollouts showed autoscaler thrash triggered by aggregated probe failures. Existing tickets addressed probe fanout and synthetic warmups but left probe thresholds static. We also have telemetry hooks in Console for per-route latency and token-level cost; we will consume those signals. Prior relevant work: ENG-4921, ENG-20345, ENG-31877.

Key goals: 1) Reduce autoscaler oscillation during transient events. 2) Maintain SLOs (p99 latency and error-rate) across multi-region failover windows. 3) Ensure safe rollback and observability for debugging.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Probe adaptation service deployed behind feature flag that dynamically adjusts readiness gating window and failure thresholds based on a short-term (1-5m) latency histogram and SLO burn rate.
2) Simulation harness reproduces 3 failure patterns (traffic spike, cross-region latency spike, partial regional outage) and shows >=25% reduction in scale-up/scale-down churn compared to baseline.
3) No increase in p99 latency or error-rate in steady state (0% regression within 95% CI over a 24h test).
4) Console dashboard added showing probe adjustments, SLO burn rate, and autoscaler decisions.
5) Canary rollout plan documented and runbook updated with rollback criteria.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Simulation & model: implement a simulator ingesting request traces + synthetic region partitions to test candidate adaptation policies (windowing, hysteresis scaling, confidence thresholds). Expected 2w.
Phase 2 - Probe adapter service: lightweight control plane (k8s controller) that watches health signal streams and writes per-deployment readiness overrides via existing readiness API. Initial policy: token-bucket smoothing + burn-rate thresholding + minimal hysteresis. 3w.
Phase 3 - Integrations: hook the adapter to metrics pipeline (Console latency histograms and SLO burn-rate endpoint), add audit logs and RBAC. 1w.
Phase 4 - Canary & tuning: deploy to a small subset of regions and routes; run traffic-mirroring experiments, collect data, iterate on thresholds. 2w.
Tasks:
- Build and validate simulator with replay harness (ENG-903210-1)
- Implement probe-adapter controller and API shim (ENG-903210-2)
- Add smoothing/hysteresis library shared with autoscaler (ENG-903210-3)
- Create observability surfaces (dashboards/alerts) (ENG-903210-4)
- Document runbook and canary steps (ENG-903210-5)
monitoring_and_metrics:
Primary metrics to observe: autoscaler scale events/min, scale oscillation index (custom), readiness-fail-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency by route, SLO burn rate (1m/5m), circuit-breaker activations, regional failover duration.
Dashboards: per-region probe-adapter adjustments, before/after autoscaler decisions, simulation comparison charts.
Alerts: if probe-adapter causes >3x increase in readiness-fail-rate or p99 latency increases beyond 10% over baseline during canary, auto-disable feature flag and page oncall.
test_plan:
Unit tests for policy math and hysteresis. End-to-end tests in staging: run simulator scenarios against shadow autoscaler to ensure no regressions. Chaos test: introduce 10% packet loss between region pairs to validate resilience. Performance test: ensure probe-adapter adds <50ms median decision latency and scales to communicate with 5000 readiness targets per minute.
Simulation acceptance: run 100 randomized episodes per scenario and compare key metrics to baseline. Document seed and inputs for reproducibility.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged internal dev cluster deploy. 2) Canary to 5% of traffic for non-critical routes in primary region for 48h. 3) Expand to 25% across two regions for 72h with extra monitoring. 4) Full rollout with gradual expansion and automated rollback on alert.
Rollback criteria: sustained p99 latency regression >10% for 30m, or autoscaler thrash spike >2x baseline within 15m.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: adapter mis-tuning could mask real readiness failures and increase error rates. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, safety net that never marks pods healthy if liveness fails, strict audit logs, and an emergency disable flag.
Risk: added control plane latency. Mitigation: keep adapter async and memoize decisions per deployment for short TTLs.
Risk: noisy SLO signal leads to flip-flopping. Mitigation: use burn-rate smoothing and minimum decision windows.
notes:
- Preference for job owners: runtime infra + serving teams collaboration.
- Keep changes backward-compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments; adapter should have a no-op mode.
- Consider later extension: let customers opt-in to adaptive probes at per-customer tier in Dedicated.
- Cross-reference incident timeline in postmortem doc: drive.google.com/drive/failover-postmortem (internal).
